## The problem

Maintainers hand-assign one of roughly 1,300 Work Unit Codes to every KC-135 maintenance record. Miscoded records reduce the quality of reliability, sustainment and readiness analysis built on that data.

## Approach

Records from two extracts (2019-2026) were merged and deduplicated. Discrepancy and corrective-action text feeds a ModernBERT-large classifier over 1,251 codes, trained with class-weighted cross-entropy and hierarchical system/subsystem auxiliary losses. The served model was then evaluated on held-out records, with accuracy reported separately from label coverage, calibration by confidence band, and errors broken down by the WUC hierarchy.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Why it matters for a decision

Supports the WUC coding decision on completed maintenance records. The top-3 suggestions plus a confidence band send low-confidence records to QC review. The confusion pairs found (for example, codes used interchangeably across bases) are direct feedback to data owners on inconsistent coding that distorts downstream analysis.
:::

## Results

| Result | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Top-1 accuracy 0.903 (95% CI 0.899-0.908) and top-3 0.978 on the 15,636-record held-out test split, scored against QC labels | training/batch_predict.py on data_splits/test.parquet after the pooling fix; recorded in CLAUDE.md and GLIDEPATH.md. The CI is computed by the auditor from recorded n. |
| 98.3% of predictions fall in the correct aircraft system; 62.8% of errors are same-subsystem near misses | training/error_analysis.py; counts (1,330 errors = 835/226/269 of 15,876) recorded in CLAUDE.md, arithmetic consistent |
| Label coverage 93.2% of records; end-to-end top-1 0.854 including records whose code is outside the model's label space | training/batch_predict.py --exclude-seen; 15,876 of 17,041 records answerable; recorded in CLAUDE.md |
| Predictions shown at 70% confidence or higher (93% of answerable records) are correct 94.6% of the time (n=14,795) | training/batch_predict.py calibration-by-band output recorded in CLAUDE.md; band counts sum to 15,876 |
| Re-measuring the serving path found a silent train/serve pooling mismatch that had cut production top-1 accuracy from 0.897 to 0.756 for three months | training/check_pooling.py; fix and guard in training/train_hierarchical.py (classifier_pooling='cls'); documented in CLAUDE.md |
| Flat and hierarchical variants are statistically indistinguishable (38 vs 29 wins on 67 one-sided disagreements, sign test p = 0.33) | training/compare_models.py on 2,000 seeded test rows, recorded in CLAUDE.md; p-value recomputed by auditor |

Every result above is traced to a script, log, or artifact in the repository. See [How I Check My Work](/approach.qmd).

## Limitations

- Accuracy is scored against QC-pipeline labels from the same process that produced the training labels. It has not been checked by a KC-135 subject-matter expert (a 25-case adjudication is pending), and the direction of any label-noise bias is unknown.
- The split is random by record with exact-text deduplication only. It has no temporal holdout and no grouping by job control number, so near-duplicate leakage may inflate accuracy, and performance on future records is untested.
- Built for post-fix coding: inputs include the corrective action. It is not a pre-repair predictor.
- 6.8% of records carry codes excluded from the label space (fewer than 5 training examples), so the model cannot predict them.
- Single training seed; no run-to-run variance reported.
- Training data and model weights are CUI and are not public; results cannot be reproduced externally.
- The LLM-written profile narrative (Tab 3) can state details that are not in the data.

## Tools

Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, ModernBERT-large, scikit-learn, pandas, Streamlit, Altair, Ollama (Gemma 4, local)
